title: Simultaneous small chunks of a simplicial model category
statement:
Use simplicial and combinatorial model categories, projective diagram models, and smallness as in [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus], and Bergner cofibrancy as in [lem-coef-simplicial-inversion-universal-property]. A chunk $U$ of a combinatorial simplicial model category $\mathcal A$ means a full simplicial subcategory with the following two closure properties, with choices functorial by simplicially enriched functors. For each finite family $X\to Y_i$ in $U$, its product map factors as a trivial cofibration $X\to Z$ followed by a fibration $Z\to\prod_iY_i$, with $Z\in U$. For each finite family $Y_i\to X$ in $U$, its coproduct map factors as a cofibration $\coprod_iY_i\to Z$ followed by a trivial fibration $Z\to X$, with $Z\in U$. Empty families are included. Put $U^{cf}=U\cap\mathcal A^{cf}$. For a small simplicial category $I$, an $I$-chunk is a chunk $U$ such that the full subcategory $U^I$ of diagrams with all values in $U$ is a chunk of the projective model category $\mathcal A^I$.

The full category $\mathcal A$ is an $I$-chunk of itself for every small $I$. Given a small family $(I_\alpha)$ of small cofibrant simplicial categories and a small full subcategory $V\subseteq\mathcal A$, there exists a small full subcategory $U\subseteq\mathcal A$ containing $V$ which is an $I_\alpha$-chunk for every $\alpha$. It can be chosen with the same essential image as $V$ in the ordinary homotopy category $\mathcal A[W^{-1}]$, where $W$ denotes its model weak equivalences.

source.place: Definitions A.3.4.1 and A.3.4.9, Example A.3.4.4, and Lemma A.3.4.15 with its construction, printed pp.885,888,890-891. Empty finite families give replacements remaining inside the chunk. Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this simplicial homotopy-theoretic result.

proof.text: For any small $I$, [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus] makes $\mathcal A^I$ a combinatorial simplicial model category, as is $\mathcal A$ itself. In either such category $\mathcal M$, choose the small generating set $J$ of each of its two model weak factorization systems. Check the tensor hypothesis of [lem-coef-enriched-functorial-factorizations]: for $j\in J$ and $p$ in the corresponding right class, the simplicial model axiom [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus] makes the map from lifts to commutative squares a trivial Kan fibration (either $j$ or $p$ is also a weak equivalence). Every simplicial set $K$ is cofibrant because $\varnothing\to K$ is degreewise injective [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Consequently every $K$-parameterized square lifts; by tensor adjunction this says that $K\otimes j$ has the left lifting property against every such $p$, hence belongs to that system's left class. Apply the generic enriched small-object node to both generating sets. Its $L,R$ are exactly the model classes because the systems are generated by these sets. This gives enriched factorizations of both types for all arrows, without endpoint cofibrancy assumptions. Factor each finite product map by the trivial-cofibration/fibration functor, and each finite coproduct map by the cofibration/trivial-fibration functor. Their middle objects lie in the whole category, so $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal A^I$ satisfy both chunk conditions. The family-to-arrow operations are enriched by universal properties: $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(T,\prod Y_i)=\prod\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(T,Y_i)$ degreewise using tensors of $T$, and $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(\coprod Y_i,T)=\prod\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(Y_i,T)$ using cotensors. Empty products and coproducts are included. Thus the full category is an $I$-chunk.

source.place: Definitions A.3.4.1 and A.3.4.9; Example A.3.4.4; enriched small-object input: Riehl Theorem 13.2.1.

proof.text: Adjoin to the small indexing family the one-object simplicial category $I_*=\mathbf1$, with mapping set $\Delta^0$, so that $\mathcal A^{I_*}=\mathcal A$; the same closure procedure will then impose the chunk conditions in $\mathcal A$ itself. By [lem-coef-small-family-regular-bound], applied to the object sets of all these shapes together with an extra copy of $\mathbf N$, choose a small uncountable regular cardinal $\kappa$ strictly larger than their disjoint union. In particular each $I_\alpha$ has fewer than $\kappa$ objects. The additional shape is used only through the identity identification $\mathcal A^{\mathbf1}=\mathcal A$; no new cofibrancy hypothesis is needed for its projective model.

source.place: Lemma A.3.4.15, adjoining the unit category and choosing a regular cardinal.

proof.text: Fix once and for all two enriched middle-object functors $F_\alpha,G_\alpha$ on the arrow category of each projective model $\mathcal A^{I_\alpha}$, using the projective models of [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus] and applying [lem-coef-enriched-functorial-factorizations] to their two generating sets, with the tensor hypotheses checked in step 1. Write their factorizations as $f\xrightarrow{\sim\;\mathrm{cof}}F_\alpha(u)\twoheadrightarrow g$ and $f\rightarrowtail G_\alpha(u)\xrightarrow{\sim\;\mathrm{fib}}g$ for $u:f\to g$. Their evaluation maps in $\mathcal A$ are weak equivalences on the indicated weak-equivalence legs, since projective weak equivalences are objectwise. The choices are global, independent of the closure stage; we will only restrict them.

source.place: Lemma A.3.4.15, first proof paragraph, enriched factorization functors.

proof.text: Define an increasing sequence of full simplicial subcategories $V_\beta$ for $\beta<\kappa$. Start with $V_0=V$. At a nonzero limit take the union of the preceding object sets and the full simplicial subcategory on that union. At a successor $\beta+1$, retain all objects of $V_\beta$ and add every $F_\alpha(u)(i)$ for all finite families $f\to g_j$ of diagrams valued in $V_\beta$, where $u:f\to\prod_jg_j$, and every $G_\alpha(v)(i)$ for all finite families $f_j\to g$ valued in $V_\beta$, where $v:\coprod_jf_j\to g$, for every $\alpha$ and $i\in I_\alpha$. Include empty families. The products and coproducts are taken in $\mathcal A^{I_\alpha}$, not in $V_\beta$; no closure of $V_\beta$ under their values is asserted. Set $U$ to be the full simplicial subcategory on $\bigcup_{\beta<\kappa}\operatorname{Ob}(V_\beta)$.

Each $V_\beta$ and $U$ is small. Indeed, for a small object set $S$ in $\mathcal A$ and a small $I_\alpha$, the set of enriched diagrams with values in $S$ is a subset of the set of object assignments together with simplicial maps between the small mapping sets, subject to the unit and composition equations. Transformations form a set as well, being families of component arrows satisfying naturality equations. There are thus only a small set of finite families and their factorization values to add at a successor. At limits, and finally at $\kappa$, take a small union of small object sets. Full mapping simplicial sets remain those of $\mathcal A$, hence small. Transfinite induction proves the assertion, and $V\subseteq U$ by construction.

source.place: Lemma A.3.4.15, details of smallness in the final sentence.

proof.text: Fix $\alpha$ and a finite family of diagrams valued in $U$ of either variance required for a chunk. Each value of each diagram belongs to some $V_\beta$. There are fewer than $\kappa$ such values, since there are finitely many diagrams and $|\operatorname{Ob}(I_\alpha)|<\kappa$. Regularity gives a common $\beta<\kappa$ containing them all. (For an empty object set of $I_\alpha$, take $\beta=0$.) Fullness then places the diagrams and their transformations in $V_\beta^{I_\alpha}$. The successor rule places every value of the chosen middle diagram in $V_{\beta+1}$, and $\beta+1<\kappa$. Hence the chosen middle diagram is valued in $U$. This also treats a family with no arrows: its distinguished source or target diagram is still among the diagrams just bounded.

source.place: Lemma A.3.4.15, regularity argument implicit in the final sentence.

proof.text: Restrict the fixed functors $F_\alpha,G_\alpha$ to the finite families valued in $U$. Step 6 shows that their middle diagrams belong to $U^{I_\alpha}$. For each fixed finite family shape, the middle-object functor has object values in this full simplicial subcategory, so its maps on mapping simplicial sets restrict to it and preserve the same identities and composition. The two factorization legs remain enriched natural transformations in the ambient projective category: the product or coproduct endpoint need not belong to $U^{I_\alpha}$. Their naturality equations are the original equations of the global factorization, restricted to families valued in $U$. The factorization classes are still those of the projective model, as supplied in steps 1 and 3 by applying [lem-coef-enriched-functorial-factorizations] to the generated model classes of [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus]; no model structure on $U$ is claimed. Thus $U^{I_\alpha}$ satisfies both chunk conditions. The adjoined one-object shape proves the same for $U$ in $\mathcal A$, so $U$ is an $I_\alpha$-chunk for every original $\alpha$. Using global restrictions, rather than stagewise choices, supplies enriched functoriality even for transformations whose endpoints first appeared at different stages.

source.place: Definitions A.3.4.1 and A.3.4.9; Lemma A.3.4.15, final closure assertion.

proof.text: Finally, prove by transfinite induction that every object of $V_\beta$ has the same image in $\mathcal A[W^{-1}]$, up to isomorphism, as some object of $V$. The base is immediate, and a limit adds no objects outside earlier stages. A newly added $F_\alpha(u)(i)$ receives the evaluated weak equivalence from $f(i)\in V_\beta$; a newly added $G_\alpha(v)(i)$ has the evaluated weak equivalence to $g(i)\in V_\beta$. These maps are weak equivalences because projective weak equivalences are objectwise [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus]. Their inverses exist by the definition of localization. Compose the resulting isomorphisms with those supplied by the induction hypothesis. Every object of $U$ belongs to a stage, so $U$ adds no essential image; $V\subseteq U$ gives the reverse inclusion. For $V=\varnothing$ the same construction adds no objects: the nonempty shapes have no distinguished diagrams, while the empty shape has no evaluations to add.

source.place: Lemma A.3.4.15, moreover clause and weak-equivalence legs in its construction.

lean.statement: theorem simplicial_small_chunks {A : Type w} [Category.{u} A] [ModelCategory A] [SimplicialCategory A] (T : SimplicialTensorCotensor A) (hC : CombinatorialModelCategory.{w, u, u} A) (hSM7 : SimplicialModelLocalization.SatisfiesSM7 A) (B : BergnerModelData.{u}) : (∀ (I : Type u) [Category.{u} I] [SimplicialCategory I], ∃ U : SimplicialChunk A, U.carrier = Set.univ ∧ ∃ (E : SimplicialDiagramEnrichment I A) (P : ProjectiveSimplicialModelStructure T E), IsIChunk U T I E P) ∧ (∀ (J : Type u) (I : J → CoherentNerve.SCat.{u}), (∀ α : J, @IsCofibrant _ _ B.model.categoryWithCofibrations (B.model.cm1b.out (Discrete PEmpty)) (I α)) → ∀ (V : ObjectProperty A), ObjectProperty.Small.{u} V → ∃ U : SimplicialChunk A, ObjectProperty.Small.{u} U.carrier ∧ V ≤ U.carrier ∧ (∀ α : J, ∃ (E : SimplicialDiagramEnrichment (CoherentNerve.underlying (I α)) A) (P : ProjectiveSimplicialModelStructure T E), IsIChunk U T (CoherentNerve.underlying (I α)) E P) ∧ U.carrier.map (MorphismProperty.Q (weakEquivalences A)) = V.map (MorphismProperty.Q (weakEquivalences A)))
